page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores across two threads per core, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and features no dedicated GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage while offering a 20 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5.16xlarge as a solid multi-core platform with moderate per-core throughput. Single-threaded performance lands in the lower tier, as evidenced by a single-core Geekbench score of 1039.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1286.19. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads leverage the 64 vCPUs effectively, achieving 54159.82 on stress-ng multi-core and 11161.0 on Geekbench multi-core. PassMark extended instruction metrics demonstrate strong execution at 52045.17, enabled by AVX-512 support. Memory performance is robust under large-block uncached read operations, delivering 192.72 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reaches 36.27 GB/sec and Redis operations sustain approximately 50.81 million SET operations per second.

The instance provides high parallel resource density, but architects must account for its architectural tradeoffs. Because single-thread execution and LLM text generation metrics show weak relative performance, workloads highly sensitive to serial latency or single-core execution speed may experience bottlenecks. Furthermore, the absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates network-attached storage architectures. Given its broad multi-core capacity, consistent DDR4 memory throughput, and 20 Gbps baseline networking, the m5.16xlarge serves enterprise backends, distributed data caching, medium-to-large relational databases, compilation clusters, and balanced web serving fleets.
description: The Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8175M processor operating at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, the server pairs its compute resources with 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates no bundled local storage and includes no discrete graphics hardware, operating over a 20 Gbps baseline network connection powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark data shows average multi-core processing throughput, supported by strong large-block memory read bandwidth of 192.72 GB/sec and solid AVX-512 instruction processing. However, single-core processing and serial tasks perform in the lower quartile. The m5.16xlarge is suited for multi-threaded enterprise application backends, relational databases, caching layers, software compilation clusters, and high-throughput web serving.
